findings.title: User docs do not describe the new step 4a baseline read of propose and ff
findings.recommendation: docs/workflow-engine.md:100 says /orbit:propose and /orbit:ff 'repeat that' (continue's status -> instructions -> read dependencies -> write loop), which since 2.0.2 is no longer the whole of it: both now read the baseline specs before proposal.md and copy MODIFIED blocks whole at the specs artifact, while /orbit:continue does not. docs/commands.md's /orbit:propose entry (lines 53-64) lists what propose does beyond writing artifacts (validate, fingerprints, draft PR) but not the read. Add one clause to each (e.g. after line 100: 'and before writing proposal.md they read the baseline spec of each capability the change modifies'), so the user-facing docs match the CHANGELOG's 2.0.2 entry.
findings.reproduction: sed -n 94,101p docs/workflow-engine.md; sed -n 53,64p docs/commands.md — neither names the baseline read the CHANGELOG's ## 2.0.2 entry announces.

findings.title: Edited Purpose sentence parses ambiguously
findings.recommendation: 'which is preserved when no exploration exists apart from the orbit steps that run in both modes' can be read as 'no exploration exists apart from the orbit steps'. Set the exception off: 'which is preserved when no exploration exists, apart from the orbit steps that run in both modes:' (a comma before 'apart'), matching the MODIFIED scenario's own comma ('behaves as upstream, apart from ...').

commentary: Probed: the full diff from the change-start commit with the trail excluded; both template edits against the fence (byte-identical, placed between the dependency-read and create lines, backticks escaped); the generated .claude skills (both carry the lines after update --force); consume mode, which still runs upstream Step 4, so the read fires in the architect -> explore -> propose path and not only in standalone; schema.yaml's 'MODIFIED requirements workflow' heading, which the specs line points at and which ships with the package, so an adopter's body points at something it has; orbit-conventions' Generated-file disposition (the delta names the step and the replacing requirement, no additions text restates it); the fingerprint check on the carried block (verified); the scenario declarations on the new test, including the moved-lines and removed-line failure cases, which genuinely exercise checkBody; residue of the retired standalone phrasing ('unchanged from upstream', 'ONE addition') across specs, src, test and docs (only the parity comment recording the move remains); version sites (all five at 2.0.2, --version prints 2.0.2, the remaining 2.0.1 strings in CLAUDE.md are historical). The build and the full suite pass, and validate --strict and validate --sources are clean. Task 3.5 is the only unchecked task and is user-validation by design. Passes 4 and 5 were skipped because orbit/lenses/ is absent. Pass 6 (audit-drift) was not invoked as a library; the targeted residue sweep above stands in for it on this change's surface only. Risk texture: the change is a two-line instruction plus a release bump, with no engine code, so the main risk is the one the design already names: the instruction can be ignored. That is the measure stage's question, not this pass's.

direction.reasoning: The implementation matches the requirement exactly: both bodies carry the fenced lines where step 4a reads context, a test that was shown able to fail holds them to the owner's fence, and the standalone requirement now tells the truth about the both-mode steps. Nothing found changes behaviour or contradicts a baseline. The two notes are documentation polish and can be taken at the walk or left. Move toward archive and the release-tree cut.
